The following lemma characterizes Pythagorean triples and is used repeatedly.\n    23\t\n    24\t <Lemma 1> If $a, b, c$ are positive integers with $ab \\neq 0$ satisfying $a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}$, then there exist positive integers $m \\neq n$ and $k$ such that\n    25\t\n    26\t \\[\n    27\t (a, b, c)=k\\left(2 m n, m^{2}-n^{2}, m^{2}+n^{2}\\right) \\text { or } k\\left(m^{2}-n^{2}, 2 m n, m^{2}+n^{2}\\right).\n    28\t \\]\n    29\t\n    30\t In particular, if $a, b$ are relatively prime, then $k=1$ and $m$ and $n$ have different parity, and one of $a, b$ is odd and the other is even.
